bilingual.notes: Two distinct add-ons: Bilingual Specialization (ACTFL OPI/OPIc Advanced Mid+ only) and Dual Language Specialization (Commission-approved program + transcripts + language proficiency exam). Schema rolls up to the broadest pathway (Bilingual Specialization), which is exam-only.

eld.notes: ESOL is a PCR (Program Completion Report) pathway endorsement: approved program is the gating credential. ORELA ESOL test is the Commission-adopted subject-matter measure; Multiple Measures-ESOL worksheet (2024) lets EPPs document equivalent competency via coursework + clinical observations + partial test score, but does not remove the test as the default.

history.title: Oregon Seal of Biliteracy adopted
history.description: Oregon adopted a State Seal of Biliteracy on 2016-04-14 (per sealofbiliteracy.org/state/or/). Awarded to graduating high school students who demonstrate proficiency in English plus one or more additional languages.

history.title: Senate Bill 13 — Tribal History/Shared History enacted
history.description: Governor signed Senate Bill 13 (codified at ORS 329.494) directing the Oregon Department of Education to develop a curriculum on the histories, languages, and contemporary lives of the nine federally-recognized tribes in Oregon, and requiring every school district to teach the curriculum at grades 4, 8, and high school. SB 13 funds tribal-language preservation work and shapes the content basis for ODE's Indigenous-language teacher-preparation work and the cultural-and-linguistic-diversity competencies that the Oregon Model Core Teaching Standards apply to all teachers. While not an EL-credential statute, SB 13 is the most significant pre-2019 Oregon language-policy enactment.

history.title: EPAA 29(100) document analysis (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021)
history.description: Leider, Colombo & Nerlino published in Education Policy Analysis Archives 29(100) a comprehensive document analysis of every state and DC's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI teacher-credentialing requirements, professional teaching standards mentions, and EL-percentage figures, based on primary SEA sources collected October–December 2019. The 2019 coding of Oregon's EL-credentialing landscape is preserved as a temporally-anchored research baseline against which the catalog's later verifications are framed.

history.title: TSPC endorsement and specialization rules effective
history.description: Teacher Standards and Practices Commission rules governing Adding Endorsements and Adding Specializations took effect 2023-11-01. ESOL remains a Program Completion Report endorsement; Bilingual Specialization continues as the broadest pathway requiring ACTFL OPI/OPIc Advanced Mid+ but no approved program; Dual Language Specialization requires an approved program.

history.title: Multiple Measures-ESOL endorsement testing option approved
history.description: TSPC approved a Multiple Measures-ESOL Endorsement Testing Option Worksheet (Commission approval June 2024, rev. 9/13/2024) documenting equivalent competency pathways: at least 20 semester / 30 quarter hours aligned with ESOL standards plus practicum or completion of a TSPC-approved ESOL program.

elPercentHistory.note: Oregon Department of Education, fall snapshot (68,038 EL students). Oregon-reported figures run roughly 0.5-1.0 percentage points above NCES across fall 2018-2020 (e.g., 2018-19 SEA 9.2% vs NCES 8.2%), with the gap narrowing to about 0.1 percentage points in 2020-21; the divergence likely reflects Oregon's inclusion of students in post-exit monitoring (NCES does not count them) or a snapshot-date difference. The 3.1 percentage-point increase from NCES's fall 2021 value (9.5%) to ODE's fall 2024 figure tracks documented enrollment growth, but the SEA series cannot be treated as methodologically continuous with NCES.
